title: Line-by-Line Narrative Comments
pattern: Inline comments preceding almost every single statement in a routine, translating code mechanics directly into prose.
why_bad: Visual scanning impediment and redundancy. Line-by-line comments repeat obvious syntactic statements, cluttering files and hiding the actual logic behind unnecessary text.
detection: Three or more consecutive lines of code where each line (or every statement block) is immediately preceded by a single-line comment translating the code.
counterexample: Statements grouped into logical paragraphs with blank lines, with at most one intent comment per paragraph.
fix: Delete the line-by-line comments; organize statements with blank lines into paragraphs of logical intent.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32.2 ("Optimum Number of Comments"); John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 13.2 ("Red Flag: Comment Repeats Code").
